issue_context.title: Add fsspec support to DuckDB
issue_context.body:
[`fsspec`](https://filesystem-spec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/?badge=latest) was initially created to abstract over various filesystem implementations for dask and pyarrow, and it makes reading from various object stores really easy, and very pluggable

I'm built a test of it integrating it with DuckDB, and although there is a perf cost due to the bindings being largely written in Python, I believe the convenience is worth it. Below is an example of what using it looks like:

```py
import logging
import duckdb
from adlfs.spec import AzureBlobFileSystem

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

connection = duckdb.connect()

connection.register_filesystem(AzureBlobFileSystem(account_name='azureopendatastorage'))

query = connection.execute(
    '''
    select *
    from read_parquet('abfs://nyctlc/green/puYear=2019/puMonth=*/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=true)
    limit 10
    '''
)

print(query.fetchall())

connection.unregister_filesystem('abfs')
```


Some bindings are missing the `modified`, which we want to use for the object cache. I've raised some PR's to fix that, so don't need to introduce that knowledge into our code
- https://github.com/fsspec/adlfs/pull/381
- https://github.com/fsspec/gcsfs/pull/516

Additionally, we can probably add a fsspec "extra" (a python packaging concept) to make installing this stuff easier
